name: Letter-by-letter sweep word list
notes: Whole words a person actually types, each of which expand.py turns into one corpus entry per keystroke. Correctly spelled on purpose: the frozen 90 already ask what happens to a typo, and this file asks the question nothing else does — whether typing a real word from its first letter to its last is ever hijacked on the way. Hebrew leads because the clitic readings are where that happens: HebrewMorphology.splits invents a stem out of the letters typed so far, and a word invented at letter four is a word the space bar can commit at letter four. `context` defaults to empty, which is the cleanest control (no sentence signal, pure lexicon); the entries that carry one are there because the sentence is part of the case. `intended` defaults to `word` and is only spelled out where the two differ.
